page.layout: One column of italic verse, five stanzas. Below the last line, at the foot: a signature "D" at centre-left and the catchword "Vincula," at right. No page number or running head printed.

p.i: Pocula sunt vitrei fontes, nam caetera rerum Munera quae pressis secum aduexere carinis Fontus habet, sed forte nemus dum cuncta per altum Luminibus lustrant, praedae quo ducit egentes Importuna fames, procul in conualle reducta Populeas inter frondes sub monte lacunam Stare vident, fluuioque anates innare loquaci. Ollis picta rubet ceruix, argentea canent Pectora, nec certa variantur tergora pluma.

Ilicet aere cauo tormenta imitantia fulmen Corripiunt, coelum ruere, & iuga visa moueri Intremuitque palus & iam resupina per vndas Corpora voluuntur miserarum infixa natantum Accingunt praedae iuuenes, viridique sub vmbra Instaurant epulas, dapibusque explentur opimis.
Interea Ductor cum iam deserta per alta Omnia lustrasset late loca, littora postquam Desolata videt, populisque vacantia Regna.
Vlterius pelago gentes penetrare repostas Constituit notisque iterum se offerre periclis Tantus amor cultus vanorum abolere Deorum Haec illum cura una dies noctesque fatigat.

Protinus irato quassatas aequore naues Componunt solidisque trabum compagibus armant Materiam sylua alta dabat, pars fontibus vrnas, Pars naues vrnis, pomisque agrestibus implent, Pars clauos, cuneosque nouant, labefactaque firmant

page.notes: Stanza breaks follow the indents; the printed long s is rendered as s. The text is set in italic throughout. Line 2 of the second stanza and the first line of the first stanza are read from a slightly blurred scan but are legible.
